items.text: Five of its seven legislators voted against the government's annual budget and two abstained. That budget added no new funding for the public dental plan, public drug coverage, or subsidized child care.
Its legislators introduced two bills to bring mental health and addiction services under the universal public insurance that covers doctor and hospital care.

Its leaders twice publicly demanded that the government sign public drug coverage agreements with all remaining regional governments, release the funding promised for them, and finish the first phase of that program.
Its new leader called for funding to extend public drug coverage nationwide after the government's spring economic update added none.
Its new leader campaigned for the leadership on keeping the existing universal public health insurance and extending it to prescription drugs and to dental, vision, hearing, and mental health care.
